scenes.heading: Solving linear equations
scenes.sub: Negatives, fractions and decimals — same method
scenes.say: Negative four x plus seven equals thirty-one. In Year 7 you solved equations like this without the negative. This year we add negatives, fractions and decimals, and the method still works.
scenes.caption: −4x + 7 = 31. In Year 7 you solved equations like this without the negative. This year we add negatives, fractions and decimals, and the method still works.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Pass-the-parcel: the last layer on is the first layer off
scenes.science: Undo the last operation done to x first, and work inwards
scenes.breaks: a parcel unwraps in one order only, but some equations can be solved correctly in more than one order.
scenes.say: Think of pass-the-parcel. The last layer of paper wrapped on is the first one you tear off. In an equation, x is the prize, and each operation is a layer. Undo the outside layer first and work your way in.

scenes.heading: The rules
points: Do the same thing to BOTH sides
Divide by the coefficient, sign included
A fraction line acts like brackets
scenes.say: Here are the rules. Do the same thing to both sides. Undo the operations in reverse order. Divide by the whole coefficient, including its sign. Treat a long fraction line like brackets. And always check in the original equation.

scenes.heading: Build up, then undo
scenes.say: First the top row: start with x, times three, divide by five, add two, and you get eleven. Now the bottom row undoes it in reverse. Eleven take away two is nine. Nine times five is forty-five. Forty-five divided by three is fifteen. So x is fifteen.
scenes.caption: Top row: start with x, × 3, ÷ 5, + 2, and you get 11. Bottom row undoes it in reverse: 11 − 2 = 9, 9 × 5 = 45, 45 ÷ 3 = 15. So x = 15.

scenes.heading: A negative coefficient
scenes.question: Solve −4x + 7 = 31.
scenes.say: Solve negative four x plus seven equals thirty-one. Subtract seven from both sides: negative four x equals twenty-four. Now divide by negative four, not four. That gives x equals negative six. Check: twenty-four plus seven is thirty-one.
scenes.caption: Solve −4x + 7 = 31. Subtract 7 from both sides: −4x = 24. Now divide by −4, not 4. That gives x = −6. Check: 24 + 7 = 31.

scenes.heading: The minus belongs to 3x
scenes.question: Solve 20 − 3x = 8.
scenes.say: Solve twenty minus three x equals eight. The minus belongs to the three x. Subtract twenty: negative three x equals negative twelve. Divide by negative three: x equals four.
scenes.caption: Solve 20 − 3x = 8. The minus belongs to the 3x. Subtract 20: −3x = −12. Divide by −3: x = 4.

scenes.heading: A fraction
scenes.question: Solve (2x − 1)/3 = 7.
scenes.say: Solve two x minus one, all over three, equals seven. The whole top is divided by three, so multiply both sides by three first: two x minus one equals twenty-one. Add one: two x equals twenty-two. Divide by two: x equals eleven.
scenes.caption: Solve (2x − 1)/3 = 7. The whole top is divided by 3, so multiply both sides by 3 first: 2x − 1 = 21. Add 1: 2x = 22. Divide by 2: x = 11.

points: Undo in reverse order: last on, first off
Keep the sign with the coefficient
scenes.say: Quick recap. Undo the last operation first. Keep the sign with the coefficient. A fraction line works like brackets. And always check your answer. Now try the practice questions!
